item_verdicts.title: IEEE-754 + - * / are bit-portable across engines; Math transcendentals are spec-level 'implementation-approximated' — so the seed-7 fingerprint is per-engine-build, not cross-browser
item_verdicts.why: All three spot-checked sources say what is attributed. MDN verbatim: 'Many Math functions have a precision that's implementation-dependent. This means that different browsers can give a different result. Even the same JavaScript engine on a different OS or architecture can give different results!' Bugzilla 1775254 title is exactly 'Improve Math.pow accuracy for large exponents' (RESOLVED FIXED), reports Math.pow(10,208)=1.0000000000000004e+208 (4 ULP), names the internally-maintained fdlibm fork, and notes Chrome shows similar ULP errors at other exponents — i.e. engines diverge, which is the claim's point. conor.computer/blog/falcon-and-floating-point exists and gives exactly Math.tan(1e16) = -1.2451734357184066 (Node) vs -1.245173435718406 (Safari). Repo side: tests/determinism.test.ts spawns two child `npx vitest run tests/determinism-probe.test.ts` processes and cross-checks both against duelFingerprint(7) in the parent — all same V8 build, no cross-engine assertion; grep for 'cross-browser|browser-portable|deterministic across browsers' across src/, tests/, docs/, RESUME_HERE.md returns nothing, so ALREADY_DONE (no defect today) holds. The Math.round(x*256) quantization in tests/utils/duel-bot.ts's fold is real, as described. Only nit, non-load-bearing: bug 1775254 is fixed, not an open tracker.

item_verdicts.title: The ONLY transcendentals on gameplay-state paths are Math.hypot and Math.atan2 — replaceable with spec-exact compares when cross-engine determinism is actually needed
item_verdicts.why: The named call sites are all real and correctly located: src/core/Sim.ts stepKunai `Math.hypot(moved.pos.x - player.pos.x, moved.pos.y - player.pos.y) <= DEFLECT_RADIUS`, src/core/projectile.ts spawnProjectile (`Math.hypot(aim.x, aim.y)`) and projectileHits (`<= PROJECTILE_HIT_RADIUS`), src/core/vec.ts len, src/core/gesture.ts `Math.atan2(Math.abs(net.y), Math.abs(net.x)) <= DIAG_RAD`. Rune's article does list hypot and atan2 on its patch list (verified verbatim), and src/core/CLAUDE.md really does mandate 'ZERO numeric literals. No allowlist — not even 0 or 1', so the config-constant caveat is right. Two factual errors: ringGeometry is NOT a sim path (only importer is src/core/artPlan.ts, an art/render plan), and the enumeration of gameplay hypot sites is incomplete, which makes the '~4 call sites deletes the entire cross-engine risk surface' claim false. ADAPT-at-Stage-5/6 survives; the scope claim does not.
item_verdicts.correction: Strike 'ringGeometry' from the sim-path list — it is imported only by src/core/artPlan.ts (art/render). And do NOT claim the squared-compare swap 'deletes the entire cross-engine risk surface of the sim in ~4 call sites'. Two further Math.hypot paths feed gameplay state and are NOT fixable by squared comparison, because they sum square roots before comparing to a threshold: (1) DrawnStroke's `resample()` accumulates `dist(prev, cur)` against RESAMPLE_SPACING, and its output points ARE the cutPoints handed to resolveSlash — every landed hit depends on them; (2) gesture.ts's launch-vs-jump split is `polylineLength(points) < LAUNCH_FLICK_MAX_LEN`, where src/core/geometry.ts polylineLength sums `dist()` → vec.len → Math.hypot. A cross-engine-lockstep prerequisite therefore also needs an exact-op length policy for stroke resampling and polyline length (e.g. fixed-point/integer accumulation, or an exactly-rounded Math.sqrt-based dist), not just the four radius/angle swaps.

item_verdicts.title: Lookup tables / polynomial sin-cos inside core: REJECT — every Math.sin/cos in the repo is render-side pose math that never feeds gameplay state
item_verdicts.why: The REJECT verdict itself survives a direct attack. I checked the one way it could have been wrong: Sim.hitboxOf returns a plain axis-aligned box built from `f.pos.x ± f.halfW` / `f.pos.y ± f.halfH` — no pose, no rotation, no trig — so pose output genuinely never reaches a hitbox. Sim.ts's import list contains no './anim' and no './fighterAnimator'; src/core/fighterAnimator.ts (the only consumer of anim.ts's easing/oscillators) is imported solely by src/game/EncounterScene.ts, a render scene. So tables/polynomial sin in core buys zero determinism, exactly as argued. But the supporting claim text is inaccurate in two checkable places, and the 'REQUIRED READING' file it names is one of them.
item_verdicts.correction: Two fixes to the claim text (verdict unchanged): (1) src/core/composePose.ts contains NO Math.sin/cos at all — its only Math reference is `Math.PI` in a degrees→radians conversion at the rotationRad line. The core sin/cos sites are src/core/anim.ts (walk swing/bob, breathe) and src/core/planPose.ts (`const cos = Math.cos(part.rotationRad)` / `const sin = Math.sin(...)`); render-side sin/cos also live in src/game/DuelScene.ts, src/game/banners.ts and src/game/samurai.ts. Add that anim.ts's easeOutCubic uses Math.pow — another implementation-approximated op, likewise render-only. (2) The duel-bot fold is not 'hp and pos.x' only: it folds `ev.type.length` for every drained event plus player.hp, enemy.hp, player.pos.x AND enemy.pos.x each frame — pos.y and Focus are the actual omissions.

item_verdicts.title: mulberry32 quality: author-flagged bias is irrelevant at duel scale — keep it, do not swap to sfc32/SplitMix32
item_verdicts.why: bryc/code discussion #21 confirms the attributed content: Ettinger states Mulberry32 'isn't equidistributed, so it doesn't produce all possible 32-bit values, and actually can't produce about 1/3 of all possible uint32_t numbers', ~16GB of output before repeating, with sfc32/jsf32 recommended by bryc for JS specifically — matching how the research attributes each recommendation. Rune's article confirms production use verbatim: 'I've used mulberry32 many times in the past so it was a pleasant surprise when I joined Rune to find us using the same algorithm.' Repo side all checks out: src/config/rng.ts carries the 'Spec-fixed (architecture mandate: "injected mulberry32 RNG, no Math.random in core/")… never "balance" them' header; src/core/rng.ts implements it; tests/rng.test.ts imports mulberry32 and pins it against a 'Canonical mulberry32 (Tommy Ettinger, public domain) — reference copy'. The portability sub-claim is verifiable from the source itself: the generator uses only `+`, `|0`, `>>>`, `^`, Math.imul and one division by UINT32_RANGE — all exactly-specified ops, so the stream is bit-portable. Only softening, not material: Ettinger presents SplitMix32 as a well-backed option rather than issuing a flat recommendation.

item_verdicts.title: Replay for PvP = seed + input tape recorded at the Sim boundary in sim-frame indices, with periodic state checksums for desync detection
item_verdicts.why: Most of the repo grounding is exact: Sim.advance(deltaMs) clamps with `Math.min(deltaMs, MAX_FRAME_MS)` and drains an owed-frames accumulator ('Scenes call ONLY this — never tick()'), src/game/DuelScene.ts and src/game/EncounterScene.ts both seed with `mulberry32(Date.now())`, and Sim.ts's applyStroke comment does record the missed Focus-spend ordering bug in the exact terms quoted ('tests/duel-baseline.test.ts did NOT catch that, because its fingerprint folds HP and position but not Focus. tests/Sim.test.ts did.') — so the fold-focusUnits instruction is well-founded and ADOPT stands. The load-bearing error is the input-surface enumeration, which would silently produce unreproducible tapes.
item_verdicts.correction: Replace 'setPlayerIntent / queueSkill / applyStroke are the ONLY mutation entry points' with the actual public mutation surface of Sim: setPlayerIntent, queueSkill, applyStroke, PLUS `requestStanceSwitch(id, to)` and `setAutoSlash(on)` — both are real player inputs wired in src/game/DuelScene.ts (requestStanceSwitch at the two stance-cycle handlers, setAutoSlash at the toggle handler) and both mutate sim state — plus `beginCombat()` as the intro→fighting transition. A tape recording only the three originally named methods cannot reproduce any duel in which the player cycled stance or toggled AUTO SLASH. Tape entries must therefore be {frame, kind: 'intent'|'stroke'|'skill'|'stance'|'autoSlash'|'beginCombat', payload}.

overall_note: Adversarial pass complete. Sources: 4 of 4 spot-checked URLs are live and say what is attributed (MDN warning quoted verbatim; Bugzilla 1775254 title/status/fdlibm detail confirmed; bryc discussion #21 confirms the 1/3-of-uint32 and ~16GB claims in Ettinger's own words; Rune confirms hypot+atan2 on the patch list and shipped mulberry32). The one grade-C source (conor.computer) reproduces the exact Math.tan(1e16) values claimed — no fabrication found anywhere. Ledger: correct as stated — docs/research/fidelity/COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md has NO RNG/determinism rows, neither §00b CORRECTIONS nor the new §S24-H 'Verify-pass corrections (2026-08-12)' block touches this area, so nothing here rests on an overturned row. Repo: every adjudication anchor exists, but three items overstate their evidence. The one finding that would cause real harm if acted on is item 5's input surface — Sim.requestStanceSwitch and Sim.setAutoSlash are player-driven mutators called from DuelScene.ts and are missing from the proposed tape, so a tape built to that spec would desync on any stance switch. Second-most consequential: item 2's claim that four call-site swaps delete the sim's whole cross-engine risk surface is false, because DrawnStroke.resample and gesture's polylineLength both sum Math.hypot distances on paths that decide where cuts land and whether a stroke is a launch or a jump — sums of square roots that squared-radius compares cannot rescue. Items 1 and 4 survive intact.
